title: feat(pm): H37 — report a family dispatch whose per-member label writes did not all land
body:
Fixes #12629

Adds **H37** to the half-state sweeper: a report-only patrol row for a family dispatch whose per-member label writes did not all land. Report-only, like every row in that file — it never writes a label, never fails a build, and its sentences say so. No existing row is weakened, renamed or re-gated; the diff is 491 added lines and 0 removed.

Based on merged `main` `d79c6025f`, which already carries H36; H37 is the next free row id.

## The predicate, and why the shared BRANCH is the whole join

The card asks to join two GitHub-side readings the patrol already makes: a **family-dispatch member pointer** on a card, or a card **named as a member in a live `Claim:` on another open card**, crossed with **that card not carrying `pm:dispatched`**.

Both halves are spelled by one string, and the protocol already writes it. The fold convention (`SKILL.md` step 4) is:

> 共享分支按链首卡命名,每张成员卡各留认领评论并点名该分支

— the shared branch is named for the chain head, and every member card leaves its own claim comment naming that branch (a member with no branch of its own is the design, not a half-state). So the roster lives in the `Branch:` directive this file has read since H20, through the existing `claimedBranches` / `governingClaim` / `branchNameTarget` helpers.

A card whose governing claim names `claude/issue-H-...` with H not its own number **is** the member pointer; a branch carrying at least one such claimant **is** a live fold; and the head is named by every member's claim, which is the second disjunct read from the other side. Nothing new is parsed.

**No prose scraping, deliberately.** A claim comment names sibling cards, serial-constraint predecessors and blocker targets as bare card refs in its own text — the claim on the filing card itself names the chain that held this script — so scanning claim prose for card numbers would manufacture members out of the one field the protocol fills in correctly. That is H20's standing call about branch spellings, applied here.

## Both directions, because both were measured

The grading comment on the card records a second instance, and a predicate reporting only the first would have said nothing about it. Per fold, the head's own state says whether the fold is in flight and every other claimant is read against it:

| head state | claimant state | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `pm:dispatched` | no `pm:dispatched` | **undispatched-member** — the filing seat's own error: a member left on `pm:queue` while the fold ran |
| closed, or open without `pm:dispatched` | `pm:dispatched` | **dispatched-residue** — the mirror instance recorded this round, a member left dispatched with its assignee after the head released |
| open, no `pm:dispatched`, some claimant dispatched | — | the **head's** own half missed; the row lands on the head and is visible only from the members' claims |
| head in neither population | any | **unresolvable-head** — declines, H19's call, never a side picked |

A fold in which nothing is dispatched at all is deliberately quiet: it is indistinguishable from an abandoned or not-yet-launched fold, and those cards are already H30's population on their own terms. Under-report over fabricate.

## Noise floor: closed, one exclusion, and it is the ordinary case

A claim naming its **own** card's branch is not fold evidence. Every solo dispatch on this board writes exactly that, so without the exclusion the row would fire on every dispatched card in existence. Nothing else is suppressed by name — there is no per-incident exclusion list to grow, which is the discipline H36's closed noise floor states.

## Bound, and its honest half

- **Round 1 is free.** It reads the claim threads the sweep already holds: every open `pm:dispatched` card (the dispatch-liveness loop) and every assigned pm-tracked card (H2's fetch). Fold *discovery* therefore converges on the open `pm:dispatched` population, exactly as the card bounds it.
- **Round 2 buys one comment page per open `pm:queue` card, and only when round 1 saw a live fold.** A board with no fold in flight costs nothing; a board with one costs at most the queue page count (40 open `pm:queue` cards at the 2026-08-24 census H30 measured, against a 15,000/h core quota and four sweeps a day). `pm:queue` is bought because that is where the dispatchable-direction lie parks, and it is the one population no other item here reads.
- **Positive evidence only.** An unread member drops out of the roster — a miss, never an invention — and the coverage pair reports it. The pass does **not** rethrow, unlike H16's and H36's: those rows *are* their detail pass, while two of H37's three directions are free and already gathered, so discarding the sweep would cost more readings than it protects. An all-failed pass is named in the summary as the transport it is.

## Pins (+59 cases; 1456 to 1515, all green)

Roster and noise floor (10) · head state, four-valued so `unknown` never reads as released (4) · the classifier asserted directly, H35's idiom (6) · the firing shape for each of the three directions (14) · silence in both directions, six cases (6) · the gathering policy, never wider than the fold it is bought for (6) · the transport judgement (3) · the render budget cap (1) · the summary coverage pair and its all-failed warning (6) · count keys on the enumerated contract, and the markdown medium (3).

**A pin caught a real bug while being written.** `branchNameTarget` returns `null` for a branch it cannot read, and `Number(null)` is `0` — a perfectly finite head number for a card that does not exist. The first draft minted a phantom fold on every unreadable branch spelling, which would then have gated the round-2 member read on nothing. The null check is now separate from the finiteness check, with the reason stated at the line.

## Ablation — five legs, each proved failable from the committed state

Method per leg: anchored occurrence counts on disk **before and after** the mutation (never the editor's exit code), the self-test run under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, then restore with `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH` proved by `git hash-object` against the HEAD blob. `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths on every leg. HEAD blob `59c23c780b2b38e4ef79d1f0bd55ecc3d78a04c4`, matched after all five.

| leg | mutation | red cases |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | drop the self-claim exclusion | 2 — both noise-floor pins |
| A2 | in-flight member always `clean` | 9 — the classifier plus every direction-1 sentence pin |
| A3 | released head always `clean` | 7 — both residue verdicts and every mirror pin |
| A4 | transport judgement always `false` | 2 — the pair pin and the summary warning |
| A5 | drop the null head guard | 1 — the phantom-fold pin above |

A4 is worth naming: its **first** run was refused by its own on-disk check and reported as **not run**, because a multi-line anchor cannot be counted by `grep -cF` (which counts lines). It was re-run with an exact substring count taken by an independent reader of the file. The guard did its job; the reading in the table is from the second run.

## Verification — derived union at head `cc68909a0`, after the final commit

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no hand-built path list; the script takes its own change set from the merge base) named 14 local gates plus the two convention obligations for a gate-script edit. All ran green, exit code captured before any pipe:

`check:agent-test-spelling` · `check:bash32-floor` · `check:cli-command-ids` · `check:cross-package-test-inputs` · `check:entry-guard` · `check:parse-guard` · `check:partof-closing-keyword` · `check:pm-half-states` · `check:pnpm-filter-targets` · `check-ci-filter-parity` · `check-closing-keyword-parity` (self-test **and** live sweep) · `check-cross-package-test-inputs` · `check-partof-closing-keyword` · `bare-root-worklist --self-test` · `check:pm-dispatch-gates` · `check:nul-bytes` · `ci-failure --self-test` (an importer of this module, which no path derivation reaches) — every one `exit=0`.

`pnpm lint` (full repo, `eslint . --no-inline-config`) also ran green — no narrowing argument needed. Verdict lines are quoted from each gate's own output.

**Not measured here, stated rather than implied:** the live sweep `node scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` exits **3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET** in this container — repo-scoped REST reads answer 403 on this seat, which is the transport class that file's own header documents. That is a refusal to run, not a failed measurement, and the sweep's behaviour on a real board is unexercised locally by construction.

## No changeset

`scripts/pm/**` publishes nothing, and the two most recent rows in this same file (H35, H36) landed with no changeset. `skip-changeset` is applied to this PR.
